subproblems.title: A Borel countably k-rectifiable set is, up to a null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces (reuse of the accepted declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces)

This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.bilipschitz_pieces-a1), reused here as step 2 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 3, 1.1–1.3).

subproblems.statement: Conventions as in the selected statement (ℝ^P = Euclid P, H⁰ = μHE[0], 𝒟^0(U) = TestFormOn U 0, 𝒟_0(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U 0, R.action(β) = ∫_M θ ξ(β) dH⁰). For all N, N' ∈ ℕ and every IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of degree 0 in univ ⊆ ℝ^N with R.measure(ℝ^N) ≠ ∞ there is a map Y assigning to every F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} a current Y(F) ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^{N'}) (domain univ) such that: (a) for every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz F, Y(F) is integer multiplicity and, for every sequence of C¹ Λ-Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} converging uniformly to F and every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N'}), R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω), where F_j^#ω(x) := (ω(F_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap(DF_j(x)); (b) if F, F' are Λ-Lipschitz and F(x) = F'(x) for H⁰-a.e. x ∈ M (μHE[0].restrict R.carrier), then Y(F) = Y(F'). (This is the selected statement for k = 0; the (IMS) antecedent is not needed in degree 0.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid N)) 0), R.measure univ ≠ ∞ → ∃ Y : (Euclid N → Euclid N') → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) 0, (∀ (F : Euclid N → Euclid N') (Λ : NNReal), LipschitzWith Λ F → IsIntegerMultiplicity (Y F) ∧ ∀ Fs : ℕ → Euclid N → Euclid N', (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (Fs j)) → (∀ j, LipschitzWith Λ (Fs j)) → TendstoUniformly Fs F atTop → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) 0, Tendsto (fun j => R.action (fun x => ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') 0) (Fs j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (Fs j) x))) atTop (𝓝 (Y F ω))) ∧ ∀ (F F' : Euclid N → Euclid N') (Λ : NNReal), LipschitzWith Λ F → LipschitzWith Λ F' → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[0].restrict R.carrier), F x = F' x) → Y F = Y F'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.6–3.9 and 2.29 specialised to n = 0, where f_#τ(M, θ, ξ) = Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)ξ(x)δ_{f(x)}; chapter-06.txt lines 770–859 and 504–523). Notation: H⁰ := μHE[0]; for a vector space E write ∅_E := (fun i : Fin 0 => i.elim0) for the empty tuple; since Fin 0 → E is a subsingleton, every 0-covector α satisfies α(v) = α(∅_E) for all v : Fin 0 → E. Let ev ∈ MultiVector N' 0 be evaluation at the empty tuple, ev(α) := α(∅) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid N') ℝ ∅, with apply_apply).
1. Counting measure. μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence for a finite set S, μHE[0](S) = #S and μHE[0].restrict S = Σ_{x∈S} δ_x (both sides give #(S ∩ T) on measurable T), so ∫_S f dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈S} f(x) for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ and ∫⁻_S g dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈S} g(x); and every infinite set has H⁰-measure ∞ (it contains finite subsets of every cardinality, each of measure equal to its cardinality by additivity over singletons).
2. The carrier is finite. R.measure(univ) = ((H⁰.restrict M).withDensity θ)(univ) = ∫⁻_M θ dH⁰ ≥ ∫⁻_M 1 dH⁰ = H⁰(M), because θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos) and M is Borel. As R.measure(univ) ≠ ∞, H⁰(M) < ∞, so M is finite by step 1. Moreover a property that holds for H⁰.restrict M-a.e. x holds at every x ∈ M: if it failed at x₀ ∈ M, the exceptional set would contain x₀, but (H⁰.restrict M){x₀} = H⁰({x₀} ∩ M) = 1 > 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' with M Borel, measure_mono).
3. Signs. By the IMRep field orients and step 2, for every x ∈ M there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q, i.e. some τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^N (necessarily τ = ∅) with ξ(x)(α) = α(∅) for all α or ξ(x)(α) = −α(∅) for all α. Choose ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} accordingly (classical choice), so ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)α(∅) for all 0-covectors α and all x ∈ M.
4. The currents. For F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} define T_F(ω) := Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)ε(x)·ω(F(x))(∅) for ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N'}) (a finite sum over the Finset M). T_F is linear in ω (the coercion of TestFormOn to forms is linear and evaluation is linear). It is sequentially continuous: if ω_j → 0 in the sense TestFormOnConverges, there is a compact K containing all tsupports with iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j → 0 uniformly on K; since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f y‖ = ‖f y‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), ω_j(y) → 0 for y ∈ K, and ω_j(y) = 0 for y ∉ K; hence ω_j(y) → 0 in the space of 0-covectors for every y, so ω_j(F(x))(∅) → 0 for each x and the finite sum T_F(ω_j) → 0. Thus T_F is a GeometricCurrentOn univ 0; set Y(F) := T_F (for every F, Lipschitz or not).
5. Actions of pulled-back forms. For any F_j and x, ((ω(F_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap(DF_j(x)))(∅) = ω(F_j x)(DF_j(x) ∘ ∅) = ω(F_j x)(∅) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply and the subsingleton property). By steps 1–3, R.action(F_j^#ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(F_j^#ω(x)) dH⁰(x) = Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)ε(x)ω(F_j(x))(∅).
6. Limit property. Let F_j → F uniformly (in particular pointwise) and ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N'}). ω is continuous (it is smooth), and evaluation at ∅ is continuous, so ω(F_j(x))(∅) → ω(F(x))(∅) for every x ∈ M; the finite sum of step 5 therefore converges to T_F(ω) = Y(F)(ω). (Neither the C¹ regularity nor the Lipschitz bound of F_j is needed in degree 0.)
7. Integrality. Fix F. For y ∈ ℝ^{N'} let c(y) := Σ_{x∈M, F(x)=y} θ(x)ε(x) ∈ ℤ (a finite sum), and M' := {y ∈ F(M) : c(y) ≠ 0}, a finite set (image of the finite M). Define R' = (M', mult', orient') by mult'(y) := |c(y)| (Int.natAbs) for y ∈ M' and 0 otherwise, and orient'(y) := −ev if y ∈ M'₋ := {y ∈ M' : c(y) < 0}, orient'(y) := ev otherwise. The IMRep fields in univ ⊆ ℝ^{N'}: M' is finite hence Borel (Set.Finite.measurableSet) and ⊆ univ; CountablyRectifiable 0 M' (M₀ := ∅, and for an enumeration y_0, …, y_{p−1} of M' the constant maps ℝ⁰ → ℝ^{N'} with values y_j, which are Lipschitz, cover M'); mult' = Σ_{y₀∈M'} |c(y₀)|·1_{{y₀}} is a finite sum of indicator functions of Borel singletons, hence measurable, and mult' > 0 on M'; ∫⁻_{M'∩K} mult' dH⁰ ≤ Σ_{y∈M'}|c(y)| < ∞ (step 1); orient' is a piecewise constant function on the finite (Borel) set M'₋, hence strongly measurable; orients: for every y ∈ M' (hence H⁰.restrict M'-a.e.), (i) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M' y ⊥ and (ii) IsUnitOrientationOf (orient'(y)) ⊥ (τ := ∅ is orthonormal with span(range ∅) = ⊥, and orient'(y)(α) = ±α(∅)).
   Proof of (i): finrank ℝ ⊥ = 0. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{N'}, ℝ) and choose ρ > 0 with f(w) = 0 for |w| ≥ ρ (compact support). Let δ := min{|z − y| : z ∈ M' ∖ {y}} > 0 (δ := 1 if M' = {y}). For 0 < r < δ/ρ, blowUpMap y r '' M' = {0} ∪ {r⁻¹(z − y) : z ∈ M' ∖ {y}} is a finite set whose points other than 0 have norm ≥ δ/r > ρ; blowUpMap y r is injective for r > 0. By step 1, ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M'} f dH⁰ = f(0) + Σ_{z∈M'∖{y}} f(r⁻¹(z − y)) = f(0), and ∫_{(⊥ : Submodule) } f dH⁰ = ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰ = f(0). So the function of r is eventually constant equal to the limit on 𝓝[>] 0.
   Represents: for ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N'}), by step 1, R'.action(ω) = Σ_{y∈M'} |c(y)|·(±1 = sign c(y))·ω(y)(∅) = Σ_{y∈M'} c(y)ω(y)(∅) = Σ_{y∈F(M)} c(y)ω(y)(∅) (c = 0 on F(M) ∖ M') = Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)ε(x)ω(F(x))(∅) (regroup the finite sum by the value y = F(x), Finset.sum_fiberwise / Finset.sum_image') = Y(F)(ω). Hence R' represents Y(F) and Y(F) is integer multiplicity.
8. Locality. If F, F' are Λ-Lipschitz and F = F' H⁰.restrict M-a.e., then by step 2 F(x) = F'(x) for every x ∈ M, so T_F(ω) = T_{F'}(ω) for every ω and Y(F) = Y(F') (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
9. Conclusion. Y := (F ↦ T_F) satisfies (a) by steps 6 and 7 (for every Λ and every Λ-Lipschitz F) and (b) by step 8. ∎
proof_key_steps: H⁰ = μH[0] is counting measure: R.measure(univ) ≥ H⁰(M) forces the carrier M to be finite, and H⁰.restrict M-a.e. statements hold at every point of M.
In degree 0 each ξ(x), x ∈ M, is ε(x)·ev with ε(x) = ±1 (unit orientation of ⊥, τ = empty tuple).
Y(F)(ω) := Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)ε(x)ω(F(x))(∅) is a continuous current; R.action(F_j^#ω) equals the same finite sum with F_j, so it converges to Y(F)(ω).

Integrality: regroup by fibres, c(y) = Σ_{F(x)=y} θε ∈ ℤ; the finite set M' = {c ≠ 0} with multiplicity |c| and orientation sign(c)·ev is an IMRep (finite sets have approximate tangent space {0}: blow-ups are eventually {0} inside any ball) representing Y(F).
Locality: equality H⁰-a.e. on M is equality on M, so Y(F) = Y(F').

subproblems.title: Orientation of an IM representation along a bi-Lipschitz parametrised piece: J_G·ξ∘G = s·(DG e) with a Borel sign s (Simon 6.3.4–3.5; step 3, (B2′), of the selected proof)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of degree k in univ ⊆ ℝ^N with Hᵏ(M) < ∞ (Hᵏ = μHE[k]). Let G : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝᵏ Borel and κ > 0 with κ|a − a'| ≤ |G(a) − G(a')| for a, a' ∈ B, G differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B, and G(B) ⊆ M. Then there is a Borel function s : ℝᵏ → ℝ with s(u) ∈ {1, −1} for every u such that, for Lebesgue-a.e. u ∈ B and every k-covector α on ℝ^N, J_G(u)·ξ(G(u))(α) = s(u)·α(DG(u)e_0, …, DG(u)e_{k−1}), where e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 and J_G(u) := (det[⟨DG(u)e_a, DG(u)e_b⟩]_{a,b})^{1/2}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (G : Euclid k → Euclid N) (B : Set (Euclid k)) (L : NNReal) (κ : ℝ), μHE[k] R.carrier ≠ ∞ → LipschitzWith L G → MeasurableSet B → 0 < κ → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, κ * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖G a - G a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ G a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ G a)) → G '' B ⊆ R.carrier → ∃ s : Euclid k → ℝ, Measurable s ∧ (∀ u, s u = 1 ∨ s u = -1) ∧ ∀ᵐ u ∂(volume.restrict B), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid N) k, Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b : Fin k => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ G u (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (fderiv ℝ G u (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))) * R.orient (G u) α = s u * α (fun a => fderiv ℝ G u (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3, Consequence (B2′), of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.4–3.5: at points where J > 0, df_x#ξ(x) = J·η with η an orienting k-vector; chapter-06.txt lines 776–806). Notation: Lᵏ := volume on ℝᵏ = μHE[k] there (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); v(u) := (DG(u)e_a)_{a<k}; J(u) := J_G(u); DG(u) := fderiv ℝ G u.
1. Pull-back of null sets. G is injective on B (κ > 0). Let ψ := Function.invFunOn G B; then ψ(G(a)) = a for a ∈ B and |ψ(y) − ψ(y')| ≤ κ⁻¹|y − y'| for y, y' ∈ G(B), i.e. LipschitzOnWith κ⁻¹ ψ (G(B)). For every Z ⊆ ℝ^N, {a ∈ B : G(a) ∈ Z} = ψ(G(B) ∩ Z), hence Lᵏ({a ∈ B : G(a) ∈ Z}) = μHE[k](ψ(G(B) ∩ Z)) ≤ κ^{−k}·Hᵏ(G(B) ∩ Z) (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). Consequences, using G(B) ⊆ M: (i) if a property p holds for (Hᵏ.restrict M)-a.e. x, then p(G(u)) holds for (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. u (apply the estimate to a Borel (Hᵏ.restrict M)-null set Z ⊇ {¬p}, e.g. toMeasurable, noting Hᵏ(G(B) ∩ Z) ≤ Hᵏ(M ∩ Z) = 0); (ii) G is quasi-measure-preserving from Lᵏ.restrict B to Hᵏ.restrict M (G is continuous, hence measurable, and Measure.map G (Lᵏ.restrict B) ≪ Hᵏ.restrict M by (i)); therefore u ↦ ξ(G(u)) is AEStronglyMeasurable for Lᵏ.restrict B (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving applied to the IMRep field aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Tangent planes. Apply the sibling piece_approx_tangent (dpf_approxTangent_ae_bilipschitz_piece) with U := univ (open), Y := M (Borel, ⊆ univ, and Hᵏ(M ∩ C) ≤ Hᵏ(M) < ∞ for every compact C), F := G, B, L, m := κ, using G(B) ⊆ M: for (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. u, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M (G u) (LinearMap.range DG(u)).
3. ξ orients the range of DG. The IMRep field orients says: for (Hᵏ.restrict M)-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. By step 1(i) this holds at x = G(u) for (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. u. Intersecting with step 2 and using the uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT Chapter03 HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), Q = range DG(u). Hence for a.e. u ∈ B: IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(G u)) (range DG(u)).
4. The normalised wedge. For u ∈ B the family v(u) is linearly independent (the standard basis vectors e_a = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin k) ℝ a are independent and DG(u) has trivial kernel: LinearIndependent.map'), and span(range v(u)) = range DG(u) (the range of a linear map on ℝᵏ is spanned by the images of a basis: LinearMap.range_eq_map, Submodule.map_span, Basis.span_eq). Define ζ_u := J(u)⁻¹ • Ev(DG(u)) ∈ MultiVector N k, where for T : ℝᵏ →L ℝ^N, Ev(T) := (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid k) ℝ e).comp (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM T) with e := (fun a => EuclideanSpace.single a 1); by apply_apply, compContinuousLinearMapCLM_apply and compContinuousLinearMap_apply, Ev(T)(α) = α(Te_0, …, Te_{k−1}), so ζ_u(α) = J(u)⁻¹·α(v(u)). By the sibling normalized_wedge_orientation (codim1_lur_normalized_wedge_orientation) with a := v(u): det Gram(v(u)) > 0, i.e. J(u) > 0, and ζ_u is a unit orientation of span(range v(u)) = range DG(u).
5. The sign. For a.e. u ∈ B, steps 3–4 and the sibling orientation_sign (rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg) give ξ(G u) = ζ_u or ξ(G u) = −ζ_u. Define s₀(u) := 1 if ‖ξ(G u) − ζ_u‖ ≤ ‖ξ(G u) + ζ_u‖ and s₀(u) := −1 otherwise (operator norm on MultiVector N k). Whenever ξ(G u) = ±ζ_u we have ξ(G u) = s₀(u)ζ_u: if ξ(G u) = ζ_u then ‖ξ − ζ‖ = 0 ≤ ‖ξ + ζ‖ and s₀ = 1; if ξ(G u) = −ζ_u and the first case fails, then ‖ξ + ζ‖ = 0 < ‖ξ − ζ‖, s₀ = −1, and ξ = −ζ = s₀ζ. Multiplying by J(u) > 0: J(u)·ξ(G u)(α) = s₀(u)·J(u)ζ_u(α) = s₀(u)·α(v(u)) for all α, for a.e. u ∈ B.
6. Measurability. u ↦ DG(u) is Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), hence strongly measurable (finite-dimensional target ℝᵏ →L ℝ^N); Ev is continuous (continuous_const.clm_comp ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM); u ↦ J(u) is Borel (part (i) of the sibling gram_area_formula, or continuity of T ↦ det[⟨Te_a, Te_b⟩] via Continuous.matrix_det, continuous_matrix and continuity of inner products, followed by Real.sqrt). Hence u ↦ ζ_u = J(u)⁻¹ • Ev(DG(u)) is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable, StronglyMeasurable.smul; this was checked in Lean at the pinned versions), and with step 1(ii) the real functions u ↦ ‖ξ(G u) ∓ ζ_u‖ are AEStronglyMeasurable for Lᵏ.restrict B, so s₀ is AEMeasurable for Lᵏ.restrict B (Measurable.piecewise on an a.e.-measurable set / AEMeasurable.ite). Let s₁ := AEMeasurable.mk s₀ (Borel, s₁ = s₀ a.e. on B) and s(u) := 1 if s₁(u) ≥ 0, s(u) := −1 otherwise. Then s is Borel, s(u) ∈ {1, −1} for all u, and s = s₀ (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. because s₀ takes only the values ±1.
7. Conclusion. For (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. u we have s(u) = s₀(u) and step 5, i.e. J_G(u)·ξ(G u)(α) = s(u)·α(DG(u)e_0, …, DG(u)e_{k−1}) for all α. The case k = 0 is included (J ≡ 1 since the Gram matrix is empty, v(u) is the empty family and range DG(u) = ⊥). ∎
proof_key_steps: Bi-Lipschitz pull-back: Hᵏ-null subsets of G(B) ⊆ M have Lebesgue-null preimages in B, so a.e. statements on M transfer to a.e. u ∈ B and ξ∘G is a.e.-strongly measurable.

dpf_approxTangent_ae_bilipschitz_piece with Y = M: a.e. u ∈ B, T_{G(u)}M = range DG(u); with the IMRep field orients and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, ξ(G u) is a unit orientation of range DG(u).
codim1_lur_normalized_wedge_orientation: ζ_u = J(u)⁻¹·(α ↦ α(DG(u)e)) is a unit orientation of the same plane and J(u) > 0.
rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg: ξ(G u) = ±ζ_u; the norm comparison s₀ = ±1 selects the sign, and J·ξ(G u)(α) = s₀α(DG(u)e).
ζ is a.e.-strongly measurable (continuous evaluation of fderiv), so s₀ is a.e.-measurable; a Borel ±1-valued modification s finishes the proof.

subproblems.title: Parametric representation of a finite-mass IM representation by bi-Lipschitz pieces with integer weights (Simon 6.3.1, 3.3–3.6 with Ch. 3, 1.1–1.3; steps 2–4 of the selected proof)
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of degree k in univ ⊆ ℝ^N with R.measure(ℝ^N) ≠ ∞. Write e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 and J_G(u) := (det[⟨DG(u)e_a, DG(u)e_b⟩]_{a,b})^{1/2}. Then there are maps G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N, sets B_i ⊆ ℝᵏ and functions w_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ (i ∈ ℕ) such that: each G_i is Lipschitz; each B_i is Borel; G_i is differentiable at every point of B_i; each w_i is Borel, integer-valued at every point, nonzero at every point of B_i, and Lebesgue-integrable on B_i; Σ_i ∫⁻_{B_i} |w_i|·J_{G_i} dLᵏ ≤ R.measure(ℝ^N); for every continuous k-form γ : ℝ^N → Λᵏ(ℝ^N)* with sup_x ‖γ(x)‖ < ∞, the series Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i(u)·γ(G_i(u))(DG_i(u)e_0, …, DG_i(u)e_{k−1}) du converges (HasSum) to R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dHᵏ; and for every predicate p on ℝ^N that holds Hᵏ-a.e. on M (μHE[k].restrict R.carrier), p(G_i(u)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. u ∈ B_i, for every i.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 and 3.3–3.6 with Ch. 3, 1.1–1.3: an integer multiplicity current τ(M, θ, ξ) is computed on Lipschitz parametrisations of M by the area formula; chapter-06.txt lines 770–820). Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]; Lᵏ := volume on ℝᵏ (= μHE[k] there, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); μ_R := R.measure = (Hᵏ.restrict M).withDensity θ, so μ_R(ℝ^N) = ∫⁻_M θ dHᵏ; for a map G, J_G is the Gram Jacobian of the statement and DG(u)e := (DG(u)e_a)_{a<k}.

Source: the partition argument of step 2 of the selected proof ('the remaining set is partitioned with Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt into Borel pieces on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz (approximation of an injective linear map with constant less than half its co-norm)'), applied in step 7 to H_i on A_i⁺; Simon Ch. 3, 1.2–1.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–75). It is steps 2–5 of the accepted proof of dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces for a single map, without the image disjointification.
1. Regular set. S := B ∩ {u : H is differentiable at u and DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u is injective}. S is Borel: {u : DifferentiableAt ℝ H u} is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), u ↦ DH(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv) and the injective maps form an open set (ContinuousLinearMap.isOpen_injective), so its preimage is Borel.
2. Coercivity radius. For each injective continuous linear T : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} choose m(T) > 0 with |Th| ≥ m(T)|h| for all h (e.g. m(T) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K T, Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith / injective linear maps on finite-dimensional spaces are antilipschitz; for k = 0 any m(T) > 0 works since ℝ⁰ = {0}). Define r : (ℝᵏ →L ℝ^{N'}) → ℝ≥0 by r(T) := m(T)/2 if T is injective and r(T) := 1 otherwise (classical choice); r(T) ≠ 0 for every T.
3. Partition. Apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := H, s := S, f' := fderiv ℝ H (for u ∈ S, H is differentiable at u, so HasFDerivWithinAt H (DH(u)) S u) and r: there are pairwise disjoint Borel t_l (l ∈ ℕ) with S ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and continuous linear T_l with ApproximatesLinearOn H T_l (S ∩ t_l) (r(T_l)), i.e. |H(a) − H(a') − T_l(a − a')| ≤ r(T_l)|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ S ∩ t_l, and, if S ≠ ∅, T_l = DH(y_l) for some y_l ∈ S.
4. Pieces. Put A_l := S ∩ t_l and κ_l := r(T_l) > 0. A_l is Borel, A_l ⊆ S ⊆ B, the A_l are pairwise disjoint (the t_l are), and ⋃_l A_l = S. Every point of A_l ⊆ S is a point where H is differentiable with injective derivative.
5. Covering. If u ∈ B, H is differentiable at u and DH(u) is injective, then u ∈ S ⊆ ⋃_l t_l, so u ∈ S ∩ t_l = A_l for some l. ∎

On A_l, |H(a) − H(a')| ≥ |T_l(a − a')| − (m/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m/2)|a − a'|; the pieces cover exactly the regular points of H in B.

Source: step 7 of the selected proof, the construction of Φ_{il} = τ(H_i(A_{il}), |g_{il}|, sign(g_{il})η_{il}) (Simon Ch. 6, 3.5–3.9: on a piece where f is injective with J > 0 the push-forward is τ(f(M_+), θ∘f⁻¹, ±η) with η the induced orientation; chapter-06.txt lines 800–859). 1. The image and the area formula. H is continuous and injective on A (κ > 0), so N := H(A) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). subproblems.statement: (i) Let k, N, N' ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} Λ-Lipschitz (Λ ∈ ℝ≥0), G : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N differentiable at u ∈ ℝᵏ. Then J_{F∘G}(u) ≤ Λᵏ·J_G(u), where J_H(u) := (det[⟨DH(u)e_a, DH(u)e_b⟩]_{a,b})^{1/2}, DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u (zero where H is not differentiable), e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1. (ii) Let k, N' ∈ ℕ, H, H' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} Lipschitz and B ⊆ ℝᵏ Borel with H = H' Lebesgue-a.e. on B. Then DH(u) = DH'(u) for Lebesgue-a.e. u ∈ B.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the selected proof ('|DH_i(u)v| ≤ Λ|DG_i(u)v| … JH_i ≤ Λ^kJG_i' and 'the derivative of a Lipschitz map at a density point of a set is determined by its values on that set') and the Jacobian bound used in step 7 (Simon Ch. 6, 2.29: M(f_#T) ≤ (ess sup |Df|)ⁿ M(T), and Ch. 2, 3.3–3.5). Notation: Lᵏ := volume on ℝᵏ; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; for a linear T on ℝᵏ, J(T) := (det[⟨Te_a, Te_b⟩])^{1/2}, so J_H(u) = J(DH(u)).
Part (i).
1. Let L := D(F∘G)(u) and M := DG(u). Claim: |Lv| ≤ Λ|Mv| for every v ∈ ℝᵏ. If F∘G is not differentiable at u, then L = 0 (fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt) and the claim is trivial. Otherwise, for t > 0, |F(G(u + tv)) − F(G(u))| ≤ Λ|G(u + tv) − G(u)|; dividing by t and letting t → 0⁺, the left side tends to |Lv| and the right side to Λ|Mv| (both maps are differentiable at u; HasFDerivAt.lim or the little-o expansion along the ray), so |Lv| ≤ Λ|Mv|.
2. If L is not injective, choose c ≠ 0 with Lc = 0; writing c = Σ_b c_b e_b, Σ_b c_b Le_b = 0, so the Gram matrix Γ_L := [⟨Le_a, Le_b⟩] satisfies Γ_L·(c_b)_b = 0 with (c_b) ≠ 0, hence det Γ_L = 0 (Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff) and J(L) = 0 ≤ Λᵏ·J(M) (J(M) ≥ 0 as a square root). (For k = 0 both Gram matrices are empty, J(L) = J(M) = 1 and Λ⁰ = 1.)
3. Suppose L is injective. Then M is injective (Mv = 0 ⇒ |Lv| ≤ 0 ⇒ v = 0). Let S := closedBall (0 : ℝᵏ) 1, so 0 < Lᵏ(S) < ∞. A continuous linear injective map T is differentiable everywhere with fderiv ℝ T x = T (ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv) and injective on S, so the sibling gram_area_formula (codim1_lura_gram_area_formula) with f := T, s := S, g ≡ 1 gives Hᵏ(T(S)) = ∫⁻_S ofReal(J(T)) dLᵏ = ofReal(J(T))·Lᵏ(S). Apply this to T = L and T = M.
4. Let λ : ℝ^N →ₗ ℝᵏ be a linear left inverse of the injective M (LinearMap.exists_leftInverse_of_injective) and A := L ∘ λ. For y = Mv, y' = Mv' ∈ M(S): |A(y) − A(y')| = |L(v − v')| ≤ Λ|M(v − v')| = Λ|y − y'| (step 1), so A is Λ-Lipschitz on M(S), and A(M(S)) = L(S). By the Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn), Hᵏ(L(S)) ≤ Λᵏ·Hᵏ(M(S)). By step 3, ofReal(J(L))·Lᵏ(S) ≤ Λᵏ·ofReal(J(M))·Lᵏ(S); cancelling 0 < Lᵏ(S) < ∞ and using J ≥ 0 gives J(L) ≤ Λᵏ·J(M), i.e. J_{F∘G}(u) ≤ Λᵏ·J_G(u).
Part (ii).
5. D := H − H' is Lipschitz and continuous, so E := B ∩ {u : D(u) = 0} is Borel and Lᵏ(B ∖ E) = 0 (hypothesis). By Rademacher (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) H, H' and D are differentiable Lᵏ-a.e.; by the Lebesgue density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for Lᵏ and E), for (Lᵏ.restrict E)-a.e. u, Lᵏ(E ∩ B̄_r(u))/Lᵏ(B̄_r(u)) → 1 as r → 0⁺. Since Lᵏ.restrict B and Lᵏ.restrict E coincide (Lᵏ(B ∖ E) = 0, E ⊆ B), for (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. u: u ∈ E, u is a density point of E, and H, H', D are differentiable at u.
6. At such u, DD(u) = 0. If k = 0 there is nothing to prove (ℝ⁰ = {0}). Let v be a unit vector and ε ∈ (0, 1). For all small t > 0 the open ball B_{εt}(u + tv) ⊆ B̄_{2t}(u) meets E: otherwise Lᵏ(E ∩ B̄_{2t}(u)) ≤ Lᵏ(B̄_{2t}(u)) − Lᵏ(B_{εt}(u + tv)) = (1 − (ε/2)ᵏ)·Lᵏ(B̄_{2t}(u)) (Haar scaling of balls, Measure.addHaar_ball / addHaar_closedBall), contradicting density 1 as t → 0⁺. Pick u_t ∈ E with |u_t − (u + tv)| < εt; then |u_t − u| < 2t and 0 = D(u_t) = D(u) + DD(u)(u_t − u) + o(t) = DD(u)(u_t − u) + o(t), so t|DD(u)v| ≤ |DD(u)(u_t − u)| + ‖DD(u)‖εt ≤ o(t) + ‖DD(u)‖εt. Dividing by t and letting t → 0⁺ gives |DD(u)v| ≤ ‖DD(u)‖ε for every ε ∈ (0, 1), hence DD(u)v = 0; as v was an arbitrary unit vector, DD(u) = 0.
7. Since H and H' are differentiable at u, DD(u) = DH(u) − DH'(u) (fderiv_sub). Hence DH(u) = DH'(u) for (Lᵏ.restrict B)-a.e. u. ∎
proof_key_steps: (i) |D(F∘G)(u)v| ≤ Λ|DG(u)v| from the difference quotients (or D(F∘G)(u) = 0 if F∘G is not differentiable at u).
(i) A non-injective linear map has singular Gram matrix, so J = 0; otherwise the area formula for linear maps gives Hᵏ(T(S)) = J(T)Lᵏ(S).
(i) L = A∘M with A Λ-Lipschitz on M(S); the Lipschitz image bound gives J(L)Lᵏ(S) ≤ ΛᵏJ(M)Lᵏ(S).
(ii) A.e. point of B is a density point of E = B ∩ {H = H'} where H, H', H − H' are differentiable (Rademacher, Lebesgue density).
(ii) At such a point every direction is approximated by points of E, so D(H − H')(u) = 0 and DH(u) = DH'(u).

Source: step 7 of the selected proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.6–3.9: f_#τ(M, θ, ξ) = τ(f(M), N, η) is integer multiplicity; chapter-06.txt lines 816–859), together with the bounds of step 6. Notation: d := k + 1; Lᵈ := volume on ℝᵈ; H_i := F∘G_i, which is (Λ·L_i)-Lipschitz if G_i is L_i-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp); f_{i,ω}(u) := w_i(u)·ω(H_i(u))(DH_i(u)e) with DH_i(u)e := (DH_i(u)e_a)_{a<d}; T_i(ω) := ∫_{B_i} f_{i,ω}; m_i := ∫⁻_{B_i} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_{G_i}) and J_i^H := J_{H_i}. By hypothesis Σ_i m_i < ∞, so every m_i < ∞.
1. Jacobian comparison. For u ∈ B_i, G_i is differentiable at u, so part (i) of the sibling lipschitz_jacobian_locality gives J_i^H(u) ≤ Λᵈ·J_{G_i}(u). Integrating over B_i (setLIntegral_mono', ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ofReal_pow): ∫⁻_{B_i} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) ≤ Λᵈ·m_i.
2. Integrability. ω is continuous with compact support, so ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ C_ω (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous); ‖DH_i(u)‖ ≤ Λ·L_i (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz) and |e_a| = 1, so |ω(H_i(u))(DH_i(u)e)| ≤ ‖ω(H_i(u))‖·Π_a|DH_i(u)e_a| ≤ C_ω(ΛL_i)ᵈ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). The function u ↦ ω(H_i(u))(DH_i(u)e) is Borel: it is the continuous map (y, T) ↦ ω(y)(fun a => T e_a) (continuous_eval for covectors) applied to the Borel pair (H_i(u), DH_i(u)) (measurable_fderiv). Since w_i is Borel and integrable on B_i, f_{i,ω} is integrable on B_i (Integrable.mono').
3. Pieces. Apply the sibling regular_partition to H_i and B_i: Borel, pairwise disjoint A_{il} ⊆ B_i and κ_{il} > 0 such that H_i is κ_{il}-bi-Lipschitz-below and differentiable with injective derivative on A_{il}, and every u ∈ B_i where H_i is differentiable with injective derivative lies in some A_{il}.
4. Piece currents. For each (i, l) apply the sibling piece_current with (IMC), H := H_i, A := A_{il}, L := Λ·L_i, κ := κ_{il}, g := w_i (Borel, integer-valued, nonzero on A_{il} ⊆ B_i), using ∫⁻_{A_{il}} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) ≤ ∫⁻_{B_i} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) ≤ Λᵈ·m_i < ∞ (step 1, lintegral_mono_set): an integer multiplicity Φ_{il} ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^{N'}) with M(Φ_{il}) ≤ ∫⁻_{A_{il}} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) and Φ_{il}(ω) = ∫_{A_{il}} f_{i,ω} for every ω.
5. Vanishing off the regular set. Let u ∈ B_i ∖ ⋃_l A_{il}. By step 3, H_i is not differentiable at u or DH_i(u) is not injective. In the first case DH_i(u) = 0 (fderiv_zero_of_not_differentiableAt), so the d ≥ 1 arguments of ω(H_i(u)) are all 0 and the value is 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_coord_zero). In the second case pick x ≠ y with DH_i(u)x = DH_i(u)y; writing x − y = Σ_a (x − y)_a e_a gives Σ_a (x − y)_a DH_i(u)e_a = 0 with coefficients not all zero, so the family DH_i(u)e is linearly dependent (Fintype.linearIndependent_iff) and the alternating map ω(H_i(u)) vanishes on it (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). Hence f_{i,ω} = 0 on B_i ∖ ⋃_l A_{il}.
6. Fibre sums. By step 5, T_i(ω) = ∫_{⋃_l A_{il}} f_{i,ω} (compare the indicator functions of B_i and ⋃_l A_{il} ⊆ B_i). By MeasureTheory.hasSum_integral_iUnion (Borel, pairwise disjoint A_{il}; f_{i,ω} integrable on ⋃_l A_{il} ⊆ B_i by step 2) and step 4: HasSum (l ↦ Φ_{il}(ω)) (T_i(ω)).
7. Masses. Σ_l M(Φ_{il}) ≤ Σ_l ∫⁻_{A_{il}} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) = ∫⁻_{⋃_l A_{il}} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) (lintegral_iUnion) ≤ ∫⁻_{B_i} ‖w_i‖ₑ·ofReal(J_i^H) ≤ Λᵈ·m_i (step 1).
8. The series current. Let π := Nat.pairEquiv.symm : ℕ ≃ ℕ × ℕ and X_r := Φ_{π(r)} ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^{N'}). Each X_r is integer multiplicity, and Σ_r M(X_r) = Σ_{(i,l)} M(Φ_{il}) (Equiv.tsum_eq) = Σ_i Σ_l M(Φ_{il}) (ENNReal.tsum_prod) ≤ Σ_i Λᵈ·m_i = Λᵈ·Σ_i m_i < ∞ (step 7, ENNReal.tsum_mul_left). (IMS) with P := N', m := k, U := univ (open) and X yields an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^{N'}) with HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)) for every ω.
9. Identification. Transporting along π (Equiv.hasSum_iff), HasSum ((i, l) ↦ Φ_{il}(ω)) (Y(ω)) on ℕ × ℕ; together with the fibre sums of step 6, HasSum.prod_fiberwise (ℝ is a regular space) gives HasSum (i ↦ T_i(ω)) (Y(ω)).
10. Per-term bound. Let c > 0 with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ c for all x. (a) covectorEuclideanNorm(t•α) = |t|·covectorEuclideanNorm(α) (unfold the definition: the square root of a sum of squares of evaluations; Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs). (b) For any X ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^{N'}) with M(X) ≠ ∞ and s = ±1, the form (s·c⁻¹)•ω is admissible for M(X) = X.massOn univ (tsupport ⊆ univ and coefficient norm ≤ c⁻¹·c = 1), so ofReal(s·c⁻¹·X(ω)) ≤ M(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, linearity map_smul), i.e. s·X(ω) ≤ c·M(X).toReal; hence |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X).toReal. (c) Each M(Φ_{il}) < ∞ (step 7) and the real series of step 6 converges absolutely, so |T_i(ω)| = |Σ_l Φ_{il}(ω)| ≤ Σ_l |Φ_{il}(ω)| (norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm) ≤ Σ_l c·M(Φ_{il}).toReal (Summable.tsum_le_tsum; the right side is summable by ENNReal.summable_toReal) = c·(Σ_l M(Φ_{il})).toReal (ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq) ≤ c·(Λᵈ·m_i).toReal = c·Λᵈ·m_i.toReal (step 7, ENNReal.toReal_mono, ENNReal.toReal_mul). ∎
